clue.text: Cost of maintaining high stock

blocks.note: up means high, as in prices that are up
to stock goods is to keep them in a shop

explanation.surface: An investor complains about the price of holding on to a share that is trading at a high value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maintaining high stock' reads like finance, but 'Cost of maintaining' is the definition and the stock is merely kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the ongoing expense of keeping property or equipment in good working order.

clue.text: Handy guide to the future provides a lifeline

definitions.text: Handy guide to the future provides a lifeline

blocks.clueFragment: Handy guide to the future provides a lifeline
blocks.note: surface reading: some useful manual on what is coming offers a rescue in a crisis

blocks.clueFragment: Handy guide to the future provides a lifeline
blocks.note: setter's reading: part of the hand, read by fortune tellers, which carries the crease called the life line

explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' is a pun on hand, and the lifeline is the crease palmists read to foretell how long you will live.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmists claim to read a person's destiny from the inner hand, including its so-called life line crease.

clue.text: Unprepared former agency worker starts out running errands

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: ex is a prefix meaning former, as in ex-wife
a temp is a temporary worker supplied by an agency
the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A one-time temp is now sent out on errands by the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done extempore is delivered off the cuff, without preparation or rehearsal.

clue.text: Pip has Estella concealing periods

indicators.note: the words themselves are said to conceal something, so the letters lie inside the run of the phrase

blocks.note: found across the end of Pip, all of has and the start of Estella

explanation.surface: In Great Expectations, Pip and Estella share a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Pip and Estella are the hero and heroine of Dickens's Great Expectations, which makes the clue look like a literature question.
explanation.definitionFit: Phases are distinct stages or spells of time in a process, just as periods are.

clue.text: Opera performance concealing adult point

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hold it hidden inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a turn is an act or performance on stage
A is the film classification for adult
a dot is a small point

explanation.surface: A staging of an opera is hiding some grown-up point.
explanation.walkthrough: A for adult comes from the old British film certificate for adult audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Turandot is Puccini's last opera, set in China and famous for the aria Nessun dorma.

clue.text: Basic choice for a burglar?

blocks.note: surface reading: the fundamental decision a thief faces when deciding a career
setter's reading: a set phrase offering an unnegotiable choice, which a burglar faces literally with each item, steal it or not

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is normally an ultimatum in bargaining; for a burglar it literally describes the decision about every valuable in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase states a final offer that must be accepted as it stands or rejected, with no negotiation.

clue.text: Quit when Dolce (or Gabbana) swapped ends

indicators.note: the first and last letters change places, each standing in for the other

blocks.note: Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana are the Italian fashion designers behind Dolce and Gabbana

explanation.surface: The fashion house partners trade places, and one walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: The D at the start of DESIGNER and the R at the end change places to give RESIGNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Resigned is the past tense of resign, meaning gave up a job, which is what quit means.

clue.text: Drug runner is part of ring in New Orleans, initially

indicators.note: one piece sits in the middle of the other
initially points to the opening letter of each of the place name's words

blocks.note: the first letters of the two words of the city name
an arc is a section of a circle or ring

explanation.surface: A drug smuggler belongs to a gang operating in New Orleans.
explanation.walkthrough: ARC goes between N and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Narco is informal, chiefly American, slang for a drug trafficker or a narcotics agent.

clue.text: Employs too many with ludicrous vast offers

indicators.note: something ludicrous is absurd and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A company hires far too many people by making absurdly generous job offers.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstaff a business is to give it more employees than the work requires.

clue.text: It requires assembly to make timely return amidst criticism

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way one came, so the word is read backwards
amidst means in the middle of, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: flack is a variant spelling of flak, harsh criticism
apt means well-timed or fitting

explanation.surface: A piece of kit needs putting together, and someone takes the flak for being prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It requires assembly' looks like a comment on parliament, but it describes furniture bought boxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat-pack furniture is sold boxed in pieces that the buyer must put together at home.

clue.text: Plant found in the middle of resown barren fields

indicators.note: points to the central letters of each word that follows

blocks.note: the central two letters of this six-letter word
the central two letters of this six-letter word
the central two letters of this six-letter word

explanation.surface: A weed turns up in fields that were sown again but produced nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of the three words has six letters, so its middle is a pair of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrel is a leafy herb of the dock family with a sharp, lemony taste.

clue.text: Venue satisfying audience

blocks.note: meeting, as in meeting a need or requirement, means satisfying it
the house is the audience in a theatre, as in a full house

explanation.surface: A place to perform that pleases the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting house is a building where people gather, especially Quakers for worship, so it is a venue.

clue.text: Car's accomplished performance for one that teaches itself

blocks.note: auto is short for automobile
did is the past tense of do, meaning carried out or accomplished
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A car does well in a test, as if it had learnt to drive itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s of Car's is just surface glue.
explanation.definitionFit: An autodidact is a self-taught person who learns without formal instruction from teachers.

clue.text: Poor duke regularly does turn for money

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
turning round means facing the other way, so the kept letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A down-at-heel nobleman takes a turn performing for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the common currency used by most member states of the European Union.

clue.text: Become agitated, if husband leaves? Get stuffed

indicators.note: the clue works backwards: removing the husband from the answer gives the other word, so he must be put inside it

blocks.note: to get stuffed is to eat too much
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife tells her angry husband to clear off and get stuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a subtraction in reverse: take H out of OVERHEAT and you get OVEREAT, so the solver puts H into OVEREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To overheat figuratively means to get too excited or worked up, as a heated person does.

clue.text: Prediction revealed by American chap in dream

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a hope is a dream or aspiration
Rosco is an American man's name, as in Sheriff Rosco P. Coltrane of The Dukes of Hazzard

explanation.surface: An American man has a vision of the future in his sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted name is not a stock crossword abbreviation, so the crossing letters do much of the work here.
explanation.definitionFit: A horoscope is an astrological forecast of a person's future based on the stars.

clue.text: Dead feeling is going down

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as on family trees
an emotion is a feeling

explanation.surface: Feeling numb, someone is sinking into gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A demotion is a move to a lower rank or position, a step down the ladder.

clue.text: Hand over before agreement

indicators.note: tells us the word for over is placed first, ahead of the other piece

blocks.note: done means finished or over
to deal is to hand out, as with cards

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders something ahead of signing a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand over' reads as one phrase, but the two words are clued separately and their order is swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A done deal is an arrangement that has been settled and can no longer be changed.

clue.text: Run behind float

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
aft means at the back, especially of a ship

explanation.surface: A swimmer races after a drifting object.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat buoyant platform, a simple float for crossing water.

clue.text: Millions following model company producing amusing programme

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece goes at the end

blocks.note: to sit is to pose as a model for an artist
Co is the abbreviation for company
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A modelling agency makes millions by producing a comedy show.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom, short for situation comedy, is a television or radio series made to be funny.

clue.text: Sign on embassy for those taking standard position in congress

definitions.text: those taking standard position in congress

indicators.note: on means attached after, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: a diplomatic mission is an embassy
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Diplomats sign up at an embassy for those adopting a standard stance in a political assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress here means sexual intercourse, and the missionary position is the conventional one, face to face with one partner on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeky cryptic hint: people using the missionary position during sex, the most conventional posture in lovemaking.

clue.text: In this way, salute Italian produce

blocks.note: so means thus, in this way
ave is the Latin greeting meaning hail

explanation.surface: This is how to greet goods from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white wine made in the Veneto region of north-east Italy.

clue.text: Technical script for part of film that's coming up

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them
in a down clue, coming up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: the end of film and the start of that's

explanation.surface: A screenplay for a scene in an upcoming movie.
explanation.definitionFit: HTML, HyperText Markup Language, is the coding language used to write web pages.

clue.text: Japanese hottie lived with a Guys and Dolls fan

blocks.note: was means existed or lived
taken as written
bi is short for bisexual, someone attracted to men and women alike

explanation.surface: An attractive Japanese person shared a home with a fan of the musical Guys and Dolls.
explanation.walkthrough: Guys and Dolls is a Broadway musical, but here it means men and women.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is the fiery green horseradish paste served with sushi, so it is hot Japanese food.

clue.text: On the way, carrying chicken starter in pastry

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside
a starter is what comes first, so the opening letter of the bird is used

blocks.note: en route is French, used in English, for on the way
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A cook on the move brings a chicken first course baked in pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course on the menu, but it only asks for the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: En croute is a French cookery term for food baked in a pastry crust, as in beef Wellington.

clue.text: Pitch tent here — it provides data link

indicators.note: to pitch is to throw or toss, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A camper sets up a tent at a spot with internet access.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch tent' reads as one camping instruction; Pitch is the signal and only tent here is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethernet is the standard technology for wired local networks connecting computers to share data.

clue.text: Some talk of one inspiring shelter to provide breakfast

indicators.note: talk refers to speech, so we want words that are pronounced the same as the pieces

blocks.note: a muse is a source of inspiration for an artist
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Someone talks about a poet's muse sheltering under cover to make breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a Swiss breakfast cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit, usually eaten with milk.
